0.v: Do Not Track & Global Privacy Control

1.v: Do Not Track & Global Privacy Control Opt in to honouring DNT / GPC with respectDnt: true (or the data-respect-dnt attribute). When on, events from browsers signalling either preference are dropped. The collector also checks the DNT and Sec-GPC request headers, so the preference is respected even if

How unique visitors are counted No identifier is stored. A visitor is a salted daily-rotating hash computed on the server: sha256( daily_salt + project_id + ip + user_agent ) Every input except the salt is already in an ordinary HTTP request, and none of them is stored — the IP is used to compute th
Excludes, localhost & bots

Excluding paths Skip routes with exclude (SDK) or data-exclude (script). Exact match, or prefix match with a trailing *. init({ key: 'YOUR_KEY', host: 'https://your-pulse.vercel.app', exclude: ['/admin*', '/preview', '/checkout/success'], });

Localhost & development By default Pulse does not track localhost, 127.*, ::1, *.local, or file:// pages, so your dev server never pollutes real numbers. Opt in with trackLocalhost: true or data-local when you specifically want to test the pipeline end to end.

Bot filtering The tracker skips obvious automation client-side as a cheap optimization — it checks navigator.webdriver and known headless globals (_phantom, __nightmare, callPhantom) and simply doesn't send the request. The real filtering happens on the server against a maintained bot list, at a per

Domain allow-list Because the ingest key is public, it can't be what authorizes a write. The real defense against forged events is your project's domain allow-list, configured in the dashboard. If set, the collector only accepts events whose URL hostname matches. An entry also covers its subdomains

Wire format Both the script and the npm package POST a small JSON body to /api/event as text/plain — which keeps it a CORS "simple request" with no preflight, so a pageview costs exactly one round trip. Keys are single letters because this is the hot path. POST https://your-pulse.vercel.app/api/even

Derived & stored Device, browser, OS — from the User-Agent Country & region — from edge geo headers Referrer host +

HTTP responses The client is fire-and-forget and ignores the response, so the collector stays deliberately quiet: it only distinguishes cases the site owner can act on. A status code never reveals whether a key exists, a domain is allow-listed, or a bot evaded the filter. StatusMeaningWhen 202Accept

Limits & validation Guardrails applied server-side so one caller can't bloat the busiest table in the database. Manual pageviews only Turn off auto-tracking and fire pageviews on your own terms — handy for wizards or modals you want to count as steps. <script defer data-key="YOUR_KEY" src="…/px.js" data-manual></script> <script> // later, when a step opens: pulse('pageview'); </script>
Troubleshooting & FAQ

My events aren't showing up You're on localhost — dev traffic is skipped unless you set trackLocalhost / data-local. localStorage.pulse_ignore is set in this browser — clear it with delete localStorage.pulse_ignore. Your domain isn't on the project's allow-list, so events are rejected server-side. T

0.v: My SPA only records the first page

1.v: My SPA only records the first page Your framework navigates without pushState. Use the matching framework adapter, or call pageview() on each route change.

I'm getting double pageviews Usually two initializations, or auto-tracking left on and a manual driver. Pick one: either autoPageviews: true and nothing else, or autoPageviews: false plus the router hook. init() is safe to call repeatedly, but two different drivers both firing will double-count.

0.v: Do I need a cookie banner?

1.v: Do I need a cookie banner? No. Consent requirements are triggered by storing or accessing information on a device, and by processing personal data. Pulse does neither — no cookies, no storage identifiers, no personal data retained. (This isn't legal advice, but it's the same basis Plausible and Umam

0.v: Is the ingest key a secret?

1.v: Is the ingest key a secret? No. It's public by necessity — it ships in your HTML. The domain allow-list is what protects you, not the key's secrecy.

0.v: Does the SDK slow down my site?

1.v: Does the SDK slow down my site? The script is 928 B gzipped (measured and enforced in CI), loads deferred, and sends fire-and-forget beacons. The npm package adds no network request and tree-shakes to the functions you use.

0.v: Can I self-check the payload before shipping?

1.v: Can I self-check the payload before shipping? Yes — open your browser's Network tab, filter to event, and inspect the request body. It's the wire format above, in plain text.

documents.text: How unique visitors are counted No identifier is stored. A visitor is a salted daily-rotating hash computed on the server: sha256( daily_salt + project_id + ip + user_agent ) Every input except the salt is already in an ordinary HTTP request, and none of them is stored — the IP is used to compute th

documents.title: Excluding paths
documents.text: Excluding paths Skip routes with exclude (SDK) or data-exclude (script). Exact match, or prefix match with a trailing *. init({ key: 'YOUR_KEY', host: 'https://your-pulse.vercel.app', exclude: ['/admin*', '/preview', '/checkout/success'], });

documents.title: Localhost & development
documents.text: Localhost & development By default Pulse does not track localhost, 127.*, ::1, *.local, or file:// pages, so your dev server never pollutes real numbers. Opt in with trackLocalhost: true or data-local when you specifically want to test the pipeline end to end.

documents.title: Bot filtering
documents.text: Bot filtering The tracker skips obvious automation client-side as a cheap optimization — it checks navigator.webdriver and known headless globals (_phantom, __nightmare, callPhantom) and simply doesn't send the request. The real filtering happens on the server against a maintained bot list, at a per

documents.title: Domain allow-list
documents.text: Domain allow-list Because the ingest key is public, it can't be what authorizes a write. The real defense against forged events is your project's domain allow-list, configured in the dashboard. If set, the collector only accepts events whose URL hostname matches. An entry also covers its subdomains

documents.title: Wire format
documents.text: Wire format Both the script and the npm package POST a small JSON body to /api/event as text/plain — which keeps it a CORS "simple request" with no preflight, so a pageview costs exactly one round trip. Keys are single letters because this is the hot path. POST https://your-pulse.vercel.app/api/even

documents.title: What the server does with your event
documents.text: What the server does with your event The client stays dumb on purpose. Everything below is derived on the edge from data the request already carries, then the raw inputs are discarded. Derived & stored Device, browser, OS — from the User-Agent Country & region — from edge geo headers Referrer host +

documents.title: HTTP responses
documents.text: HTTP responses The client is fire-and-forget and ignores the response, so the collector stays deliberately quiet: it only distinguishes cases the site owner can act on. A status code never reveals whether a key exists, a domain is allow-listed, or a bot evaded the filter. StatusMeaningWhen 202Accept

documents.title: Troubleshooting & FAQ
documents.text: Troubleshooting & FAQ

documents.title: My events aren't showing up
documents.text: My events aren't showing up You're on localhost — dev traffic is skipped unless you set trackLocalhost / data-local. localStorage.pulse_ignore is set in this browser — clear it with delete localStorage.pulse_ignore. Your domain isn't on the project's allow-list, so events are rejected server-side. T

documents.title: My SPA only records the first page
documents.text: My SPA only records the first page Your framework navigates without pushState. Use the matching framework adapter, or call pageview() on each route change.

documents.title: I'm getting double pageviews
documents.text: I'm getting double pageviews Usually two initializations, or auto-tracking left on and a manual driver. Pick one: either autoPageviews: true and nothing else, or autoPageviews: false plus the router hook. init() is safe to call repeatedly, but two different drivers both firing will double-count.

documents.title: Do I need a cookie banner?
documents.text: Do I need a cookie banner? No. Consent requirements are triggered by storing or accessing information on a device, and by processing personal data. Pulse does neither — no cookies, no storage identifiers, no personal data retained. (This isn't legal advice, but it's the same basis Plausible and Umam

documents.title: Is the ingest key a secret?
documents.text: Is the ingest key a secret? No. It's public by necessity — it ships in your HTML. The domain allow-list is what protects you, not the key's secrecy.

documents.title: Does the SDK slow down my site?
documents.text: Does the SDK slow down my site? The script is 928 B gzipped (measured and enforced in CI), loads deferred, and sends fire-and-forget beacons. The npm package adds no network request and tree-shakes to the functions you use.

documents.title: Can I self-check the payload before shipping?
documents.text: Can I self-check the payload before shipping? Yes — open your browser's Network tab, filter to event, and inspect the request body. It's the wire format above, in plain text.
